question: Which Linux notification backend contract should OpenClaw support for the core headless node-host `system.notify` command?
rationale: The code gap is clear, but the backend choice affects installed dependencies, security review, headless behavior, and support expectations across Linux desktop environments.

options.title: Bounded notify-send backend
options.body: Implement `notify-send` as the first argv-only backend with display-session detection, clear unavailable results, dependency docs, tests, and Linux desktop proof.

options.title: Broader D-Bus/dunstify fallback
options.body: Support direct D-Bus or `dunstify` fallback now, accepting more code and security review for broader desktop coverage.

options.title: Defer to Linux companion app
options.body: Keep headless node-host notifications unsupported and let the broader Linux companion app direction own desktop notification UX later.

recommendation.title: Bounded notify-send backend
recommendation.body: Implement `notify-send` as the first argv-only backend with display-session detection, clear unavailable results, dependency docs, tests, and Linux desktop proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The issue discussion and VISION/platform direction route this product choice through the Linux/node platform boundary Peter has been shaping.
